name: Centrifugal pump
howTo: Check NPSH / suction strainer — How: measure suction pressure and compare to required NPSH per manufacturer manual, remove and clean suction strainer. Tools: suction/discharge pressure gauges, wrenches, cleaning brush. Safety first: pump locked out, isolated, depressurized and PPE worn. Done when: suction pressure above minimum per manufacturer manual and strainer clean with steady flow and no cavitation noise.

Inspect mechanical seal flush — How: inspect flush piping, filter/orifice and sight glass for flow, leaks and blockage and verify pressure per manufacturer manual. Tools: flashlight, pressure gauge, wrench, clean cloth. Safety first: pump locked out and cooled with spill containment in place. Done when: clear steady flush flow at pressure per manufacturer manual with no leaks or overheating at seal.

Check alignment and bearing condition (ISO 10816) — How: check coupling alignment and tighten to torque per manufacturer manual, measure bearing vibration per ISO 10816 and check temperature and lubrication. Tools: dial indicator/laser alignment tool, vibration meter, IR thermometer, grease gun. Safety first: pump locked out with coupling guard refitted after check and PPE worn. Done when: alignment and vibration within limits per manufacturer manual and ISO 10816 with smooth quiet bearings and no overheating.

name: Positive-displacement pump
howTo: Verify relief valve setting — How: confirm lift pressure with calibrated gauge and adjust only to setpoint per manufacturer manual. Tools: calibrated pressure gauge, basic hand tools. Safety first: pump locked out, depressurized, and isolated from system. Done when: valve lifts at set pressure per manufacturer manual and reseats without leak.

Inspect check valves — How: remove, clean, and inspect balls/poppets, seats, and springs for wear or debris, torque fasteners per manufacturer manual. Tools: basic hand tools, cleaning cloths, inspection light. Safety first: pump locked out, depressurized, and drained. Done when: seats seal cleanly with no backflow, wear, or sticking.

Check pulsation dampener charge — How: isolate and depressurize pump side, then check pre-charge with gauge and recharge to pressure per manufacturer manual. Tools: air/gas pressure gauge, charging pump/hose. Safety first: pump locked out and fully depressurized before checking charge. Done when: pre-charge holds at pressure per manufacturer manual with no leak.

name: Submersible pump
howTo: Megger motor cable — How: isolate and disconnect cable, then test phase-to-earth and phase-to-phase insulation per manufacturer manual. Tools: insulation resistance tester, multimeter. Safety first: power isolated, locked out, and proven dead. Done when: readings are stable and above minimum per manufacturer manual.

Check level cut-out — How: raise and lower float / simulate level to verify start and stop levels per manufacturer manual. Tools: multimeter, water level simulator or manual lift. Safety first: power isolated for adjustment, then live test with guards in place. Done when: pump cuts in and cuts out at setpoints per manufacturer manual.

Inspect impeller for debris — How: lift pump, remove cover, clear debris and check for damage, tighten fasteners per manufacturer manual. Tools: lifting gear, hand tools, cleaning brush, torch. Safety first: power isolated and locked out, pump drained and clean. Done when: impeller clear, undamaged, and rotates freely per manufacturer manual.

name: Compressor
howTo: Check intercooler — How: Visually inspect for fouling, leaks, and corrosion and check temperature differential per manufacturer manual. Tools: inspection lamp, thermometer, pressure gauges. Safety first: compressor stopped, isolated, and depressurized. Done when: clean, leak-free, and cooling performance within limits per manufacturer manual.

Verify anti-surge valve — How: Check valve movement, actuator response, and setpoints per manufacturer manual. Tools: hand tools, calibration test equipment. Safety first: compressor in safe shutdown with control power isolated as required. Done when: valve strokes freely and opens/closes at settings per manufacturer manual.

Inspect valve plates — How: Remove covers, inspect plates and springs for cracks, wear, and deposits, clean seats, and retighten to torque per manufacturer manual. Tools: hand tools, torque wrench, cleaner, inspection lamp. Safety first: compressor locked out, isolated, and depressurized. Done when: plates seal properly with no damage and fasteners torqued per manufacturer manual.

name: Gas/steam turbine
howTo: Test overspeed trip — How: perform electronic/mechanical overspeed trip test per manufacturer manual procedure. Tools: tachometer, control panel test switch. Safety first: turbine unloaded and stable with personnel clear of rotating parts. Done when: trip actuates at set speed per manufacturer manual and resets normally.

Inspect combustors/nozzles — How: remove covers and visually/borescope inspect liners, nozzles and fasteners, tighten to torque per manufacturer manual. Tools: borescope, hand tools, torque wrench, flashlight. Safety first: unit shutdown, cooled, fuel isolated and lockout/tagout applied. Done when: no cracks, burning, clogging or distortion beyond limits per manufacturer manual.

Check lube oil — How: check level, pressure, temperature and condition against settings per manufacturer manual, top up or sample as needed. Tools: sight glass/dipstick, gauges, oil sample bottle. Safety first: wear PPE and check with unit in state per manufacturer manual, beware hot surfaces. Done when: level and pressure in normal range per manufacturer manual with clean oil and no leaks/alarms.

name: Induction motor
howTo: Measure phase currents — How: Clamp each phase conductor at the starter with motor at normal load and record all three readings. Tools: clamp ammeter, PPE. Safety first: energized work by qualified person only with guards secured. Done when: currents are balanced and within nameplate FLA per manufacturer manual.

Megger windings — How: Isolate motor, disconnect leads and test phase-to-earth and phase-to-phase at test voltage per manufacturer manual. Tools: insulation resistance tester, discharge lead, PPE. Safety first: locked out, tagged out, verified dead and fully discharged. Done when: readings are above minimum per manufacturer manual and logged.

Grease bearings per schedule — How: Clean grease fitting and add specified type and quantity per manufacturer manual with grease gun. Tools: grease gun, correct grease, lint-free rag. Safety first: motor stopped and isolated unless per manufacturer manual requires rotation with guards on. Done when: correct amount added per manufacturer manual with no over-greasing and fitting wiped clean.

name: Gearbox
howTo: Oil analysis — How: draw warm oil sample from sample valve after flushing a small amount into waste container. Tools: sample pump/bottle, clean sample bottle and label, gloves. Safety first: gearbox stopped, isolated, and oil cool enough for safe handling. Done when: labeled sample sealed with no spills and level topped up per manufacturer manual if needed.

Check backlash — How: mount dial indicator against gear tooth and gently rock shaft to read movement and compare to per manufacturer manual. Tools: dial indicator with magnetic base, hand tools. Safety first: lockout-tagout with zero rotation confirmed. Done when: backlash measurement recorded and within per manufacturer manual.

Inspect seals and breather — How: clean exterior and visually check seals for leaks and remove breather to check for blockage. Tools: flashlight, lint-free rags, soft brush. Safety first: machine isolated and surfaces cool to touch. Done when: no active leaks, breather clear and refitted tightened per manufacturer manual.

name: Isolation valve
howTo: Repack gland — How: isolate valve, remove gland follower, pick out old packing, install new packing rings with joints staggered per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrenches, packing pick, new packing. Safety first: valve isolated, depressurized and vented. Done when: gland tightened per manufacturer manual with no stem leakage and free stem movement.

Lap seats — How: disassemble valve, clean disc and seats, apply lapping compound and rotate to lap per manufacturer manual, clean fully and reassemble. Tools: wrenches, lapping compound, lapping tool, lint-free cloths. Safety first: valve isolated, depressurized and parts cleaned. Done when: even matte contact pattern and leak-tight closure retorqued per manufacturer manual.

Exercise valve — How: slowly operate valve fully closed to fully open and back per manufacturer manual. Tools: handwheel or hand wrench only. Safety first: confirm system permits operation with stable pressure. Done when: smooth full travel without sticking and correct open/closed position reached.

name: Shell & tube heat exchanger
howTo: Trend approach temperature — How: Record hot-side and cold-side inlet/outlet temperatures daily and calculate approach temperature per manufacturer manual. Tools: calibrated thermometers/RTDs, log sheet. Safety first: System in normal operation with guards closed and PPE worn. Done when: Trend is stable and within limits per manufacturer manual.

Pressure test tubes — How: Isolate, drain, and pressurize tubeside to test pressure per manufacturer manual and watch gauge for drop. Tools: hydrostatic test pump, calibrated pressure gauge, blinds/plugs. Safety first: Exchanger isolated, depressurized, drained, cooled, and locked out. Done when: Pressure holds per manufacturer manual with no drop or visible leaks.

Clean bundle — How: Remove covers, pull bundle, brush and flush tubes, then reinstall and tighten per manufacturer manual. Tools: soft tube brushes, low-pressure hose, non-corrosive cleaner, wrenches. Safety first: Locked out, depressurized, drained, cooled with gloves, goggles and chemical PPE. Done when: Tubes visibly clear, bundle reinstalled leak-free and performance restored.

name: Boiler
howTo: Test low-water cut-off — How: slow-drain test to low-water trip point per manufacturer manual and verify burner shutdown and alarm. Tools: bucket, hand tools, multimeter. Safety first: boiler attended in test mode with PPE to avoid steam and hot water burns. Done when: burner shuts off at low-water level with alarm on and resets normally on refill.

Inspect burner/igniter — How: visually inspect, clean deposits, check gap and position per manufacturer manual and observe trial ignition. Tools: soft brush, rags, feeler gauge, screwdrivers. Safety first: fuel and power locked out, boiler cool and ventilated with no fuel odor. Done when: igniter is clean and aligned with strong spark and smooth burner light-off.

Check water chemistry — How: take cooled sample and test pH, TDS or conductivity, and hardness against limits per manufacturer manual. Tools: sample bottle, water test kit and strips, log sheet. Safety first: cool and depressurize sample line slowly with gloves and eye protection to prevent scalding. Done when: results are within range per manufacturer manual and recorded with treatment adjusted if needed.

name: Belt conveyor
howTo: Adjust training idlers — How: loosen mounting bolts and nudge training idler frame slightly to steer belt to center then retighten per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrenches, pry bar, tape measure. Safety first: conveyor locked out/tagged out and tested for zero energy. Done when: belt runs centered without rubbing structure.

Check take-up tension — How: inspect take-up position and belt sag then adjust screw or gravity take-up to setting per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrenches, tape measure, belt tension gauge. Safety first: conveyor locked out/tagged out with take-up secured against sudden movement. Done when: take-up is within travel marks and belt tension is per manufacturer manual with no slip.

Replace seized idlers — How: remove clips/bolts, lift out seized idler roller, install new roller and tighten fasteners per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrenches, pry bar, replacement idler roller. Safety first: conveyor locked out/tagged out with belt supported if lifted. Done when: new idler spins freely by hand and is seated squarely.

name: Power transformer
howTo: Check oil level and DGA — How: read conservator oil level gauge and take oil sample from sampling valve for lab DGA. Tools: PPE, DGA sampling syringe/bottle kit, wiping cloth. Safety first: transformer normally energized - maintain electrical clearance with no open flames. Done when: level is in normal band per manufacturer manual and labeled sample is secured for lab.

Inspect cooling fans — How: visually check blades, guards and wiring for damage/dirt, verify auto/manual run and check mounting fasteners per manufacturer manual. Tools: PPE, flashlight, soft brush. Safety first: fans may auto-start - keep hands and clothing clear, use lockout for contact work. Done when: all fans start and run smoothly with no abnormal noise/vibration and guards secure.

Thermal scan connections — How: scan bushings, terminals and cable connections with IR camera under load from safe distance. Tools: calibrated thermal imaging camera, PPE. Safety first: equipment energized - maintain safe clearance and do not touch live parts. Done when: no abnormal hotspots and temperature rise is within limits per manufacturer manual.

name: MCC panel
howTo: Thermal scan under load — How: scan all breakers, bus joints, and cable terminations through IR window / with covers closed under normal load. Tools: calibrated IR thermal camera. Safety first: panel energized - wear arc-rated PPE, keep safe distance, do not open energized covers. Done when: no abnormal hotspots and phase-to-phase delta within limits per manufacturer manual.

Torque terminations — How: de-energize, inspect then re-torque power and control terminations to spec per manufacturer manual in sequence. Tools: insulated torque screwdriver / torque wrench, LOTO kit. Safety first: locked-out/tagged-out and verified zero energy with meter. Done when: all terminations tight to torque per manufacturer manual with no loose, frayed, or discolored conductors.

Check control voltage — How: energize control circuit and measure AC/DC control voltage at control transformer secondary and control terminals. Tools: CAT III digital multimeter, insulated probes. Safety first: wear PPE and avoid contact with live power bus, test leads one-hand where possible. Done when: measured voltage stable within rated tolerance per manufacturer manual.

name: Fire & gas detector
howTo: Bump test with certified gas — How: Apply certified test gas with calibration cap per manufacturer manual. Tools: certified test gas, regulator, calibration cap. Safety first: Inhibit fire/gas alarm outputs and inform control room. Done when: Detector alarms within time per manufacturer manual and returns to normal in clean air.

Clean optics — How: Wipe lens/window with soft lint-free cloth and approved cleaner per manufacturer manual. Tools: lint-free cloths, approved lens cleaner. Safety first: Inhibit detector outputs and de-energize per permit if required. Done when: Optics are clean, clear, and fault signal clears per manufacturer manual.

Calibrate per maker procedure — How: Zero and span calibrate using certified gas per manufacturer manual. Tools: certified calibration gas, regulator, calibration cap, multimeter per manufacturer manual. Safety first: Inhibit alarm/deluge outputs and obtain work permit. Done when: Reading matches test gas within tolerance per manufacturer manual with no fault.

name: Pressure transmitter
howTo: Blow down impulse lines — How: close transmitter isolation valves then crack drain/vent valves slowly to flush lines to safe container. Tools: wrench, drain container, rags, PPE. Safety first: transmitter isolated, drain path clear and PPE worn. Done when: steady clean flow with no sludge, air bubbles or blockage and fittings retightened per manufacturer manual.

Compare with test gauge — How: connect calibrated test gauge to test port and apply same pressure in steps across range. Tools: calibrated test gauge, pressure hand pump, fittings. Safety first: pressure kept within rated limit and connections leak-checked. Done when: transmitter reading matches test gauge within tolerance per manufacturer manual.

Check 4-20 mA loop — How: connect digital multimeter in series in loop and read output at zero and span pressure. Tools: digital multimeter, loop calibrator, screwdriver. Safety first: loop powered with covers secured and live terminals not touched. Done when: stable 4 mA at zero and 20 mA at full scale with linear response per manufacturer manual.

name: Temperature transmitter
howTo: Check RTD resistance — How: disconnect sensor leads and measure resistance with multimeter and compare to temperature vs resistance table per manufacturer manual. Tools: digital multimeter, temperature chart. Safety first: loop power isolated and de-energized. Done when: measured resistance matches expected value for ambient temperature within tolerance.

Inspect thermowell — How: visually check for corrosion, pitting, coating damage and fouling, clean as needed and verify tightness to torque per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrench, flashlight, cleaning cloth. Safety first: process isolated, depressurized and cool. Done when: thermowell is clean, undamaged, tightly seated with no leak.

Loop test — How: apply temperature simulation or drive output and verify 4-20 mA at controller with settings per manufacturer manual. Tools: temperature calibrator, loop calibrator/multimeter. Safety first: notify control room and place loop in manual/bypass. Done when: 4 mA at low range and 20 mA at high range read correctly within tolerance.

name: Level transmitter
howTo: Verify density/config — How: Check programmed fluid density, LRV/URV and units against process datasheet and correct per manufacturer manual. Tools: handheld communicator, datasheet. Safety first: Obtain work permit and do not change output in auto without operations approval. Done when: Config matches datasheet and reading is stable.

Compare with sight glass — How: Compare transmitter reading to sight glass at steady level after flushing sight glass. Tools: PPE, sight glass valves. Safety first: Check for hot/pressurized fluid and wear PPE before operating valves. Done when: Transmitter agrees with sight glass within tolerance per manufacturer manual.

Clean antenna — How: Isolate, remove sensor if needed, wipe antenna with soft lint-free cloth and reinstall and torque per manufacturer manual. Tools: soft cloth, mild cleaner, hand tools. Safety first: De-energize and follow lockout/tagout and vessel entry rules. Done when: Antenna is clean, undamaged and level reading is stable.

name: Flow transmitter
howTo: Zero at no flow — How: close block valves to ensure full pipe with no flow and perform zero trim per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrench, HART communicator. Safety first: confirm line isolated and depressurized for valve operation. Done when: transmitter reads 0 flow within tolerance.

Check straight-run — How: measure upstream and downstream straight pipe runs and compare to requirements per manufacturer manual. Tools: tape measure, inspection light. Safety first: do not open live process, inspect externally only. Done when: straight-run lengths meet minimum diameters with no disturbances.

Inspect primary element — How: remove and inspect orifice plate / averaging tube for damage or plugging and reinstall to torque per manufacturer manual. Tools: wrenches, cleaning brush, inspection mirror. Safety first: line depressurized, drained and LOTO verified. Done when: element is clean, undamaged and correctly seated with no leaks.

name: Control valve
howTo: Stroke test 0-25-50-75-100% — How: Apply 4-20 mA input in steps of 0-25-50-75-100% and back down while observing stem travel indicator. Tools: loop calibrator, travel scale/ruler. Safety first: Confirm with operations that valve movement is safe with process isolated or bypassed. Done when: Stem position tracks each step smoothly with no sticking and error within tolerance per manufacturer manual.

Check positioner air supply — How: Check supply pressure gauge, drain filter, inspect tubing/fittings for leaks with soapy water. Tools: pressure gauge, leak detection solution, clean cloth. Safety first: Keep air supply on and process in safe steady state with eye protection worn. Done when: Supply pressure is clean, dry and steady at setpoint per manufacturer manual with no leaks.

Inspect trim — How: Disassemble bonnet and inspect plug, seat, cage and stem for erosion, scoring or buildup, clean and replace damaged parts. Tools: general hand tools, soft brush, new gaskets. Safety first: Fully isolate, depressurize, drain and lockout/tagout valve before opening. Done when: Trim is clean and undamaged and bonnet reassembled and torqued per manufacturer manual with no leak on test.

name: ESD system
howTo: Review bypass register — How: review bypass register for active bypasses/inhibits and verify authorization and expiry per manufacturer manual. Tools: bypass register, HMI/panel. Safety first: confirm no required safety function is left bypassed without approved permit. Done when: register checked, expired bypasses cleared and all statuses documented.

Partial-stroke test — How: initiate partial-stroke test from control panel per manufacturer manual and observe valve movement. Tools: HMI/test switch, position indication. Safety first: confirm process is stable and test will not cause trip. Done when: valve strokes to partial position and returns with pass indication logged.

Proof-test per SIL schedule — How: perform full SIL proof-test per schedule and test procedure per manufacturer manual by simulating trip demands. Tools: proof-test procedure, calibrator/multimeter, HMI. Safety first: obtain work permit and confirm system lined up for safe full shutdown test. Done when: all ESD functions actuate correctly and results are recorded as pass.
